claims.text: The test alloy is equimolar WTaTiVZr, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
Multi-principal-element compositional disorder in WTaTiVZr produces atomic-scale lattice distortions.
Atomic-scale lattice distortions promote more uniformly dispersed dislocation glide paths.
More uniformly dispersed dislocation glide reduces crack-initiation sites.
The proposed disorder-mediated deformation increases plastic strain relative to pure tungsten at elevated plasma-facing-component temperatures.
The proposed disorder-mediated deformation enhances toughness relative to pure tungsten at elevated plasma-facing-component temperatures.
Testing WTaTiVZr and pure W with matched grain sizes, defect populations, geometries, orientations, surface finishes, and strain rates is intended to isolate the effect of composition.
A temperature range of approximately 1000–1200 °C is representative of high-temperature plasma-facing-component service.
Deformation of WTaTiVZr under the proposed conditions will involve ongoing dislocation activity.
Dislocation activity in WTaTiVZr will be more spatially uniform than slip in pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten will exhibit more localized slip and crack initiation than WTaTiVZr.
Compositional disorder in WTaTiVZr suppresses shear localization.
Compositional disorder in WTaTiVZr facilitates cross-slip.
Suppressed shear localization and facilitated cross-slip delay crack nucleation.
WTaTiVZr will show a lower crack-propagation rate than pure tungsten at the tested temperatures.
WTaTiVZr will show greater ductility and fracture toughness than pure tungsten at the tested temperatures.
Pure tungsten has useful high-temperature strength.
Pure tungsten is susceptible to brittle behavior and restricted plasticity in plasma-facing applications.
The proposed toughening effect is expected primarily when WTaTiVZr remains in a BCC high-entropy regime and is tested above the ductile-to-brittle transition.
No direct published plastic-strain or toughness data are currently available for WTaTiVZr.
